question: Which of the randomness sources named by nix-hermit-execbuilder-prototype_20260729 actually leak under `hermit run --no-namespace`, and by what mechanism?

host.note: AMD; ARCH_SET_CPUID returns ENODEV (no CPUID faulting) and PMU validation reports AmdSpecLockMapShouldBeDisabled. Neither affects these probes: no probe reads CPUID or RDTSC, and every mode is measured on the same host.

hermit.delta_vs_base: one commit, confined to `run_sabre` in hermit-cli/src/lib.rs (SaBRe backend). Unreachable from the ptrace backend used for every measurement here, so it cannot affect these results.

method.recorded_quantity: number of DISTINCT values observed across the 10 runs of one (source, mode) cell
method.relaxations: none beyond the mode under test (`--no-namespace` is itself the variable)
method.positive_control: the `native` mode must report LEAK on all five sources, proving each probe can detect variation; it does (10 distinct / 10 runs on every source)
method.guest_env: LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC exported by the harness

command: cd harness && cc -O2 -o probes probes.c && N=10 HERMIT_BIN=<hermit> ./run-matrix.sh
headline: AT_RANDOM and /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid are ALREADY determinized under --no-namespace (both prior claims refuted). getpid() is the sole primitive leak (10 distinct / 10 runs) and bash $RANDOM is its intermittent observable consequence (3 distinct / 10 runs).

supersedes_claims.claim: AT_RANDOM-seeded userspace PRNGs are not virtualized under --no-namespace; bash $RANDOM differs because it derives from AT_RANDOM
supersedes_claims.verdict: REFUTED — AT_RANDOM is byte-identical across 10 runs in both namespace modes

supersedes_claims.claim: /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid is read straight from the host kernel RNG under --no-namespace
supersedes_claims.verdict: REFUTED — identical across 10 runs; hermit intercepts the path via ProcfsKind::RandomUuid

supersedes_claims.claim: the procfs UUID probe is determinized under --no-namespace
supersedes_claims.verdict: CONFIRMED, and shown not to depend on rootless podman — it reproduces on the bare host

supersedes_claims.claim: bash seeds $RANDOM from the real host getpid()
supersedes_claims.verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — getpid is measured to be the only varying seed input, but the bash-internal seed path is NOT verified; a reimplementation of bash 5.1's documented seedrand/intrand32 did not reproduce the observed triples

limitations: The bash-internal path from getpid() to $RANDOM is inferred by elimination, not confirmed against this bash build's source or a debugger.
Only the ptrace backend was measured. KVM, DBI, SaBRe, LiteInst and e9patch were not exercised.
Single host. Cross-host reproducibility of the determinized values was not tested; only run-to-run stability on one host.
N=10 per cell. A source that varies with probability below ~10% per run could read as determinized here; `bash_random` at 3/10 shows this regime is real.
No Nix build was run in this experiment. The link to reproducible builds is inherited from the two prior experiments, not re-measured.
